breakfast.name: Nasi Katok
instructions: Cook jasmine rice in a rice cooker with a pinch of salt.
Season chicken drumsticks with turmeric, chili powder, and salt.
Coat chicken in flour and deep-fry in hot oil until golden brown and cooked through, about 12 minutes.
Serve a mound of rice topped with fried chicken and sambal belacan on the side.
breakfast.description: Brunei's beloved everyday meal of fragrant rice paired with crispy fried chicken and fiery sambal, wrapped in brown paper for a quick and satisfying bite.

breakfast.name: Kuih Mor
instructions: Mix glutinous rice flour with coconut milk and a pinch of salt to form a smooth dough.
Melt palm sugar with a little water to make a thick syrup, then let it cool.
Take small portions of dough, flatten, and fill with palm sugar syrup. Seal into balls.
Wrap each ball in a piece of banana leaf and steam for 25 minutes until cooked through.
Serve warm, rolled in freshly grated coconut.
breakfast.description: Traditional Bruneian glutinous rice cakes filled with molten palm sugar and coated in grated coconut, a sweet morning treat enjoyed with tea.

breakfast.name: Kuih Malaya (Rolled Coconut Pancake)
ingredients: Batter: 1 cup flour, 1 egg, 200ml coconut milk, pandan extract, pinch salt, green food coloring (optional)
Filling: grated coconut, palm sugar (gula melaka), pandan leaf
instructions: Make thin pancake batter with coconut milk, egg, flour, pandan
Cook filling: toast grated coconut with palm sugar and pandan until sticky
Make thin crepes from batter
Spread coconut filling on each crepe
Roll up tightly
Slice into rounds to serve
breakfast.description: Pandan-green crepes filled with sweet coconut — a beloved Malay kuih found at every Brunei morning market.

lunch.name: Ambuyat
ingredients: Assorted side dishes: grilled fish, steamed vegetables
instructions: Bring water to a rolling boil in a pot.
Gradually add sago starch while stirring vigorously with a fork or chopsticks until the mixture forms a translucent, sticky mass.
Prepare the cacah dipping sauce by mixing shrimp paste with tamarind, sugar, and chilies.
Serve ambuyat in the pot with the cacah sauce and side dishes arranged around it.
Use a bamboo fork (candas) to twirl the ambuyat and dip into the sauce.
lunch.description: The national dish of Brunei, a starchy sago-based preparation twirled on bamboo forks and dipped into tangy, savory shrimp paste sauce.

lunch.name: Soto Brunei
ingredients: Bean sprouts, fried shallots, lime wedges for garnish
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Simmer chicken thighs in chicken stock with lemongrass, galangal, and turmeric for 35 minutes until tender.
Remove chicken, shred the meat, and return broth to a simmer.
Saute shallots and garlic until fragrant, then add to the broth. Season with salt and pepper.
Cook rice vermicelli according to package directions and divide among bowls.
Ladle hot broth over noodles, top with shredded chicken, bean sprouts, fried shallots, and lime wedges.
lunch.description: A comforting Bruneian-style chicken soup with aromatic spices, rice vermicelli, and fresh garnishes, often enjoyed as a midday meal.

lunch.name: Nasi Katok
instructions: Steam rice
Fry chicken piece until golden and cooked through
Make sambal: pound chili, shrimp paste, lime juice
Serve rice with chicken and sambal
lunch.description: Brunei's national cheap meal — rice, fried chicken, sambal. Sold wrapped in paper for 1 BND at stalls across the country.

dinner.name: Rendang Daging
instructions: Combine all blended ingredients in a large pot and cook over medium heat until fragrant, about 5 minutes.
Add beef cubes and stir to coat with the spice paste.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a gentle boil. Add lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and turmeric leaf.
Reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, for about 90 minutes.
Add coconut cream and kerisik, continue cooking until the sauce is thick and dark, coating the meat.
Season with salt and sugar. Serve with steamed rice.
dinner.description: A rich, slow-cooked beef rendang with layers of spice and toasted coconut, deeply flavored and dry in the Bruneian style.

dinner.name: Udang Sambal Serai
instructions: Heat oil in a wok and saute shallots, garlic, and lemongrass until fragrant.
Add the blended chili paste and cook until the oil separates from the paste.
Toss in the prawns and stir-fry until they turn pink, about 4 minutes.
Add tamarind juice, sugar, and salt. Toss to coat evenly.
Serve immediately with steamed rice.
dinner.description: Succulent prawns wok-fried in a spicy lemongrass and chili sambal, a beloved Bruneian seafood dish with bold, aromatic flavors.

dinner.name: Soto Brunei (Spiced Chicken Soup)
instructions: Simmer chicken with lemongrass, galangal, turmeric until tender
Remove chicken, shred meat
Strain broth, return to pot
Add shredded chicken back
To serve: place vermicelli and bean sprouts in bowl
Ladle hot broth and chicken over
Top with egg halves, fried shallots, lime, sambal
dinner.description: Brunei's soul-warming chicken soup — fragrant with galangal and turmeric, loaded with toppings. A Ramadan staple.

snacks.name: Cucur Udang
instructions: Mix both flours with turmeric, chili flakes, and salt. Add water to make a thick batter.
Fold in shrimp, bean sprouts, and spring onions.
Heat oil in a deep pan. Drop spoonfuls of batter into the hot oil.
Fry until golden and crispy on all sides, about 3 minutes per batch.
Drain on paper towels and serve with sweet chili sauce.
snacks.description: Crispy Bruneian shrimp fritters packed with bean sprouts and spring onions, a popular teatime snack sold at roadside stalls.

snacks.name: Cucur Udang (Prawn Fritters)
instructions: Mix flours with turmeric, salt, and water to thick batter
Fold in prawns, chili, bean sprouts, spring onion
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil
Fry until golden and crispy
Serve with sweet chili sauce
snacks.description: Crispy prawn fritters — a teatime favorite across Brunei, always served with dipping sauce.

snacks.name: Ambuyat (Sago Starch Hot Pot)
ingredients: Dipping sauces: cacah (fermented durian/shrimp paste), tempoyak, sambal
Side dishes: grilled fish, vegetables, fried tofu
instructions: Bring water to boil
Pour boiling water into sago starch gradually, stirring with chopstick or fork
Keep stirring — it transforms into a translucent, stretchy, gluey mass
It's ready when it's completely translucent and sticky
Use a bamboo fork (candas) — twirl a ball of ambuyat around the prongs
Dip the ball into cacah sauce and eat in one go — don't chew, swallow
The texture is the challenge — it's sticky, stretchy, and unfamiliar to outsiders
This is Brunei's national dish, eaten communally from a shared pot
snacks.description: Brunei's national dish — a translucent, stretchy sago starch eaten communally with a special bamboo fork and dipped in pungent cacah sauce. The bizarre texture and twirling technique have made it viral, and the fermented durian dipping sauce divides every food creator who tries it.

desserts.name: Kuih Lapis
ingredients: Food coloring (red, green, or pandan extract)
instructions: Dissolve sugar in water over low heat, then let cool. Mix in coconut milk and salt.
Combine rice flour and tapioca starch. Gradually add the coconut sugar mixture, stirring until smooth.
Divide batter into portions and color each differently.
Grease a square tray and steam the first colored layer for 5 minutes until set.
Add the next colored layer on top and steam again. Repeat until all layers are used.
Let cool completely, then cut into diamond shapes to serve.
desserts.description: A beautiful multicolored steamed layer cake with a soft, chewy texture, a staple at Bruneian celebrations and festive gatherings.

desserts.name: Kuih Lapis (Layered Cake)
ingredients: Spice mix: cinnamon, cardamom, clove, nutmeg
instructions: Cream butter and sugar
Add egg yolks one at a time
Fold in flour and tapioca starch alternately with coconut milk
Divide batter: leave half plain (vanilla), color half with pandan
Grease a pan, pour thin layer of one batter
Grill/broil until set and lightly browned
Add layer of other batter, grill again
Repeat for 18-20 alternating layers
Cool completely before cutting — it should slice into distinct striped layers
desserts.description: Layer cake of Malay royalty — 20 thin grilled layers alternating pandan and vanilla. A labor of love served at Hari Raya.

drinks.name: Teh Tarik
instructions: Brew black tea in boiling water for 5 minutes, then strain.
Add condensed milk and evaporated milk to the hot tea.
Pour the tea back and forth between two cups from a height to create a frothy top.
Repeat the pulling motion several times until well mixed and frothy.
Serve hot in glasses.
drinks.description: Pulled tea made by pouring sweetened black tea between cups to create a creamy froth, a beloved daily drink throughout Brunei.

drinks.name: Tuak
ingredients: Bark strips from the raru tree (or substitute with a cinnamon stick for flavor)
instructions: Collect fresh coconut palm sap from the cut flower stalks of the coconut palm.
Add raru bark strips to the sap in a jar for a subtle woody flavor.
Allow the sap to naturally ferment for 1 to 3 days at room temperature.
Strain and serve at room temperature or slightly chilled.
Consume within a few days as it continues to ferment and will become more sour.
drinks.description: Traditional palm wine made from naturally fermented coconut sap, historically enjoyed by Brunei's indigenous communities during celebrations.

drinks.name: Teh Tarik (Pulled Tea)
ingredients: Strong black tea (2 tea bags or loose)
instructions: Brew very strong tea
Mix with condensed milk in a mug
'Pull' the tea: pour from one vessel to another at arm's length, repeatedly
This creates a thick foam and cools the tea
Serve immediately — the foam should sit on top
drinks.description: Tea pulled between two vessels to create thick froth — the art is in the pour. Every kopitiam in Brunei makes it.
